captions.detailed: A BMX front-end assembly featuring a grey Cr-Mo steel fork, a black head tube, and wide black riser handlebars with grips. The fork blades taper down to rectangular dropouts, while the upper steerer tube passes through a short black head tube. A grey alloy stem clamps the handlebars, which can rotate 360 degrees relative to the head tube via a continuous revolute joint.
captions.instruction: Create a 3D model of a BMX fork and handlebar assembly. The model should include a tapered grey fork with a crown, a black head tube, a grey front-load stem, and wide black riser handlebars with grips. Ensure the fork and handlebars can rotate together as a single unit relative to the head tube using a revolute joint.
captions.factory: The assembly is constructed using multiple parts connected by a revolute joint. The head tube is created as a black cylinder with a mounting bracket. The fork and handlebar assembly is defined as a single moving part: the fork blades are modeled using tapered sweeps or extruded profiles with rectangular dropouts at the tips, the crown is an extruded block, the steerer tube is a cylinder, the stem is built from boolean-joined boxes and cylinders, and the handlebars are swept along a 3D path with cylindrical grips at the ends. A continuous revolute joint is established between the head tube and the steerer tube along the Z-axis.
